notes: Taken from the Board of Elections' official candidate list and issue synopsis. Long charter amendments are condensed; the full wording is in the Board's issue synopsis and on the sample ballot.

Candidates are listed alphabetically by last name, not in ballot order: Ohio rotates the order of names from precinct to precinct. Certified write-in candidates are not printed on the ballot and are not listed.

"Where you live" uses the state voter file: a district or school levy is shown for a city, village or township when any of its voters live in that district. Your exact ballot depends on your precinct.
County Council at-large is a vote for up to three of the six candidates.

issues.title: Charter amendment: Section 101b (rental security deposits and application fees)
issues.text: Enact Section 101b to require property owners or operators to permit security deposits for residential rentals to be paid over three or six month periods; require operators to inform tenants of that right, criminalizing failure to notify; ban fees, charges, deposits or other payments before executing rental agreements; and criminalize collecting an application fee for residential rentals.

issues.title: Charter amendment: Section 100a (anti-discrimination protections; criminal history in housing)
issues.text: Enact Section 100a to add the City's existing codified anti-discrimination protections to the Charter; with exceptions for sex offenders and arson offenders, prohibit declining to rent to, or engage in real estate transactions with, an individual on the basis of criminal history, making individuals with criminal histories a protected class for renting, home sales and other real estate transactions; give the Akron Civil Rights Commission jurisdiction over real estate discrimination claims in Akron; and require City Council to enact implementing legislation within 90 days.

issues.title: Charter amendment: Section 68a (police oversight board and Independent Police Auditor)
issues.text: Amend Section 68a to change the composition and appointment process of the citizens' police oversight board (fewer Council appointees; one-third of members selected by the Board from a list provided by a committee of members of qualifying civil rights organizations); set procedures and deadlines for the Mayor, Police Chief and Council to respond to the Independent Police Auditor's recommendations; and authorize the Auditor's office to subpoena records and compel attendance and testimony.

issues.title: Local liquor option: Sunday sales, Akron 4-F (off-premises)
issues.text: Shall the sale of wine and mixed beverages, of the same types as may be legally sold in this precinct on other days of the week, be permitted in this Akron 4-F for consumption off the premises where sold on Sunday?

issues.title: Local liquor option: Oakhill Foodmart
issues.text: Shall the sale of wine and mixed beverages be permitted by Sunrise Petroleum, Inc. doing business as Oakhill Foodmart an applicant for a C2 liquor permit, who is engaged in the business of operating a full-service convenience store and foodmart at 2514 Mogadore Rd., Akron, Ohio 44312, in this precinct?

issues.title: Local liquor option: Oakhill Foodmart (Sunday)

issues.title: Charter amendment: Sections 4.02 and 6.03 (Division of Parks and Recreation)
issues.text: Shall Section 4.02 be amended to establish a Division of Parks and Recreation under the direct reporting of the Director of Public Service and shall Section 6.03 be amended to require the Parks and Recreation Commission to serve in an advisory capacity?

issues.title: Charter amendment: Section 5.11 (public posting places)
issues.text: Shall Section 5.11 be amended to remove the requirement that six (6) public places in the municipality be established if public posting is selected as the medium?

issues.title: Charter amendment: Article 7 (non-partisan municipal elections)
issues.text: Shall Article 7 be amended to require non-partisan municipal elections?

issues.title: Local liquor option: Club 2209 on the Riverfront / Barro di Mario (Sunday)

issues.title: Charter amendment: Section 4.8 (notice of special Council meetings)
issues.text: Shall Section 4.8 of the Charter of the City of Green be amended to replace the option of leaving a copy of the notice at the usual place of residence of the Mayor and Council members and substitute email with read receipt as a form of notification for special Council meetings?

issues.title: Charter amendment: Section 4.11 (publishing ordinances and notices)
issues.text: Shall Section 4.11 of the Charter of the City of Green be amended to eliminate the requirement of the posting of ordinances and resolutions and other public notices in at least five public places within the City and add the Central Administration Building, and electronic/online equivalent of a newspaper of general circulation in the City, or the City's website for 30 days as a method of publication for ordinances, resolutions, and other public notices?

issues.title: Charter amendment: Section 7.4 (Parks and Recreation Board)
issues.text: Shall Section 7.4 of the Charter of the City of Green be amended to clarify the powers and duties of the Parks and Recreation Board?

issues.title: Charter amendment: Section 8.2 (income tax allocation to parks and recreation)
issues.text: Shall Section 8.2 of the Charter of the City of Green be amended to modify the allocation of annual income tax revenue funds to the City Parks and Recreation Program?

issues.title: Charter amendment: Section 9.2 (publishing Charter Review recommendations)
issues.text: Shall Section 9.2 of the Charter of the City of Green be amended to allow Council to use the electronic/online equivalent of a newspaper of general circulation in the City as a method of publication for Charter Review Commission recommendations?

issues.title: Charter amendment: Section 9.2 (charter review every five years)
issues.text: Shall Section 9.2 of the Charter of the City of Green be amended to require the City Charter be reviewed every five (5) years?

issues.title: Natural gas aggregation
issues.text: Shall the City of Hudson, Ohio have the authority to aggregate the retail natural gas loads located in the City, and for that purpose, enter into service agreements to facilitate for those loads the sale and purchase of natural gas, such aggregation to occur automatically for eligible local utility customers except where any person is under contract or elects to opt out, all in accordance with Section 4929.26 of the Ohio Revised Code?

issues.title: Charter amendment: Article II, Section 2.09 (Mayor's salary)
issues.text: Change the Mayor's salary rate in the Charter from $11,250 to $15,000, unless otherwise approved by the voters for the next term of office.

issues.title: Charter amendment: Article III, Section 3.08 (Council salaries)
issues.text: Change Council members' salary rate from $7,500 to $10,000 and the President of Council's from $8,500 to $11,000, unless otherwise approved by the voters for the next term of office.

issues.title: Charter amendment: Article IV, Section 4.03 (Administrative Officer supervision of Finance and Law)
issues.text: Place the Department of Finance and Department of Law under the direct administrative supervision of the Administrative Officer, while preserving the existing appointment and removal provisions and the legally vested fiscal and professional legal duties of those offices.

issues.title: Charter amendment: Article V, Section 5.03.B (Board of Control contract approval)
issues.text: Raise the contract amount requiring Board of Control approval from five thousand dollars to ten thousand dollars.

issues.title: Charter amendment: Title of the chief legal officer
issues.text: Change the title of the City's chief legal officer from Solicitor to Director of Law, without changing the appointment, qualifications, powers, duties, suspension or removal provisions applicable to that office.

issues.title: Ordinance: compensation of the Mayor, Law Director and Finance Director
issues.text: Set the base annual salary of the Mayor, Law Director and Finance Director at $100,000 each effective January 2, 2028 (increases of 24%, 23% and 23% over the salaries set in 2011 and 2013), and from January 2, 2029 increase each year by no less than the aggregate of the City's collective bargaining units' annual percentage increase.

issues.title: Charter amendment: Section 3.06 (Acting Mayor)
issues.text: Amend Section 3.06 so that the President of Council, or a member of Council designated by majority vote, becomes Acting Mayor when the Mayor is temporarily absent, inaccessible or unable to serve, or until Council elects a Mayor after a vacancy; if the President of Council cannot serve as Acting Mayor, Council chooses a designee by majority vote; a Council member acting as Mayor gives up Council voting power while doing so.

issues.title: Charter amendment: new Section 6.08 (Acting Finance Director)
issues.text: Add Section 6.08 so that the Assistant Director of the General Division becomes Acting Finance Director when the Finance Director is temporarily absent, inaccessible or unable to serve; if that position is vacant, the Mayor appoints an Acting Finance Director from within the Finance Department.

issues.title: Charter amendment: new Section 9.07 (Acting Law Director)
issues.text: Add Section 9.07 so that the Deputy Law Director becomes Acting Law Director when the Law Director is temporarily absent, inaccessible or unable to serve; if that position is vacant, the Mayor appoints an Acting Law Director from within the Law Department.
